findings.action: Added a final Remarks schematic showing the open tangent ball, the restricted injective exponential map, the zero vector image p, and the boundary collision at -p. The caption specifies schematic dimensional conventions and retains the normal-coordinate identity.

diagram_math_checks.objects_maps: The left panel denotes B_pi(0_p) subset T_p S^n; the right denotes S^n. The map is exp_p:T_p S^n -> S^n, restricted to the open ball for the arrow labelled injective.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Example and Verification 1.1 define exp_p on all tangent vectors with the displayed cosine/sine formula; Verification 2.2 proves injectivity precisely for norms less than pi. The figure does not claim a new diffeomorphism or surjectivity result.

diagram_math_checks.relation: exp_p(0_p)=p; a supplied interior v maps to the point labelled exp_p(v).
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification 1.1 gives the zero branch and formula for any tangent v. Point placement is schematic and explicitly not to scale; no lengths, radial angles or dimension-specific embedding are asserted.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The marked -pi e_1 and +pi e_1 are excluded from the open ball, distinct, and satisfy exp_p(-pi e_1)=-p=exp_p(pi e_1).
diagram_math_checks.justification: Example defines the ball by |v|<pi; supplied e_1 has unit norm and n>=1. Verification 3.1 applies sin(pi)=0 and cos(pi)=-1 to both vectors, while 2.2 excludes interior collisions. Dashed source boundary and open endpoint marks enforce the strict restriction; the hollow antipode indicates the boundary image rather than an interior vector image.

diagram_math_checks.relation: For v in a normal domain D subset B_pi(0_p), x_e^i(exp_p(v))=v^i.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification 1.2 and def-normal-neighborhood-and-normal-coordinate-chart define x_e=E_e^{-1} composed with the inverse restricted exponential. Caption uses E_e^{-1}, so its domain is tangent D and codomain is the corresponding coordinate domain in R^n.

diagram_math_checks.dimensional_conventions: Disk and sphere panels are abstract schematics for n>=1; the caption explicitly says that for n=1 the ball is an interval and the sphere a circle.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The original example covers all n>=1 and excludes n=0 in Verification 3.1. No new dimensional hypothesis or projection theorem is introduced.
